## Likely Cause of the Heartburn Pattern

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

This pattern most often fits **acid reflux / GERD**: stomach acid moving up into the esophagus, especially after **large meals, coffee, and lying down soon after eating**. Occasional **ibuprofen** can also irritate the stomach and make symptoms worse.

## Practical Steps and Common Non-Prescription Options

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

| Area | What to try | Why it helps |
|---|---|---|
| Meal size | Eat smaller dinners; avoid very full stomachs | Less pressure pushing acid upward |
| Timing | Finish eating 2-3 hours before lying down | Reduces nighttime reflux |
| Coffee | Cut back, switch to smaller amounts, or try low-acid/decaf | Coffee can trigger reflux in some people |
| Trigger foods | Notice whether spicy, fatty, tomato, chocolate, mint, or alcohol worsen it | Helps identify personal triggers |
| Body position | Stay upright after meals; raise head of bed 6-8 inches if symptoms happen at night | Uses gravity to limit reflux |
| Weight / clothing | If relevant, gradual weight loss and avoiding tight waistbands can help | Lowers abdominal pressure |
| Pain relievers | Use ibuprofen less often if possible; consider asking a clinician/pharmacist about alternatives | NSAIDs can irritate the stomach |

Common OTC options people use:
- **Antacids**: quick relief for occasional symptoms; examples include calcium carbonate or magnesium/aluminum products.
- **H2 blockers**: longer relief for frequent symptoms; examples include famotidine.
- **PPIs**: strongest acid suppression; examples include omeprazole or lansoprazole, usually taken daily for a short course when symptoms are frequent.

A common approach is:
- Use an **antacid** for fast, as-needed relief.
- If symptoms happen several times a week, consider an **H2 blocker** or a **short OTC PPI course** following the package directions.
- If you need OTC medicine often, it is worth discussing with a clinician.

## When Heartburn Needs Medical Care

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

Seek medical evaluation sooner if any of these appear:
- **Trouble swallowing** or food getting stuck
- **Vomiting**, especially repeated vomiting
- **Black stools** or vomiting blood
- **Unexplained weight loss**
- **Chest pain**, pressure, shortness of breath, sweating, or pain spreading to the arm/jaw
- Symptoms that **persist beyond 2-4 weeks** despite OTC treatment
- Heartburn that is **getting worse**, waking you often at night, or happening most days

## What This Means for Your Situation

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

Given the history, the most likely explanation is **reflux triggered by large dinners, coffee, and possibly ibuprofen**. A reasonable non-emergency plan is to start with meal and timing changes, reduce triggers, and try an OTC antacid or famotidine as directed on the label. If symptoms continue for more than a few weeks or become more frequent, a routine medical visit is appropriate.
